title: Sponsorship-led catalog intake and version stability gates
creator: Aisha Rao
description: Create a sponsor-driven intake rubric and stability gating flow for new model additions, version pinning requests, and planned deprecations focused on enterprise customers. The goal is to ensure high-signal requests (enterprise / partner) have a fast-track, well-documented lifecycle while maintaining guardrails: eval requirements, pin windows, rollback policies, and deprecation runways. This ticket will define the rubric, intake form changes, required artifacts, and the handoff/playbook between PM, Eng, and Solutions teams.
acceptance_criteria: A public-facing intake form field 'Sponsor / Customer' is defined and validated; requests with a sponsor are flagged in the catalog triage queue.
A 3-tier gating rubric exists (Fast-Track, Normal, Deferred) with objective thresholds for stability, latency delta, cost delta, and eval pass rates.
Version pinning policy is defined (minimum pin window, approval steps, automatic renewal options) and documented in the onboarding playbook.
Deprecation runway templates (30/60/90-day) available for enterprise models with automated customer notifications and migration guidance.
A lightweight canary rollout checklist for new catalog models is ready for Engineering to execute with telemetry targets and rollback triggers.
Hand-off checklist with required artifacts (eval report, perf dashboard snapshot, security sign-off if applicable, sponsor approval) is in Confluence and referenced in the intake flow.
At least one sponsored model request completes the flow as a pilot and feedback gets incorporated into the rubric.
tasks: Draft sponsor-centric intake form fields and validation rules
Define objective thresholds for Fast-Track vs Normal triage
Draft version pinning lifecycle (approval, duration, renewal, metrics)
Create deprecation runway templates and notification cadence
Collaborate with Eng to author a canary rollout checklist and telemetry SLOs
Create Confluence playbook and link from intake form
Pilot flow with 1–2 enterprise requests and collect feedback
decision_log: 2026-02-12: Agreed to require both sponsor and a business-impact note for fast-track; sponsor alone is insufficient.
2026-02-18: Chose 60-day default pin window for enterprise with auto-renew opt-in — trade-off between stability and catalog churn.
2026-02-26: Decided that performance regressions >15% latency or >2x token cost will block fast-track unless mitigations are presented.
2026-03-04: Engineering proposed an automated telemetry snapshot to be captured at intake; accepted and added to required artifacts list.
risks: Fast-tracking based on sponsor may surface models that regress cost/latency for other customers — mitigated via objective thresholds and mandatory perf reports
Pinning models for long windows can bloat backend and increase operational debt — mitigation: auto-renew opt-in and pin budget review each quarter
Insufficient telemetry at intake can delay triage decisions — mitigation: require snapshot and templates
Customer expectation mismatch on deprecation timelines if communications are not standardized
notes: We want to strike a balance: enterprise customers get predictable behavior (pinning + runway) while preventing the catalog from becoming a collection of outdated pinned variants.
Design will create a 'Sponsor' badge shown in the catalog UI for models approved via this flow.
Consider adding a 'sponsorship SLA' label that drives routing to Dedicated capacity specialists when justified.
We're aligning thresholds with existing runtime SLOs — will consult Runtime Leads (Samir, Olga) before finalizing numbers.
